recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Do not restore Request/Event instantiates for FHIR-13908; any future cleanup of legacy Search worksheet rows should be handled under a separate current issue because it is distinct from this applied data-element rename/type decision.
issue_request: FHIR-13908 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 workflow issue for the Definition, Event, and Request logical patterns. It asked to remove the heavy split definitionReference/definitionUri approach, use a URI-oriented instantiates relationship for Event and Request, and, per the Jira comment, use Definition.derivedFrom for the Definition pattern.
initial_application: The Jira says the issue was pre-applied in SVN revision 12374. Git commit 5064224bd079b7f4ef4023d3ead9111b57bd8bff is the corresponding git-svn import and changed Definition.definition to Definition.derivedFrom with type uri, and Event.definition/Request.definition to Event.instantiates/Request.instantiates with type uri.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini still lists definition, event, and request as active logical models. Later R5 workflow decisions changed the current representation: FHIR-32897 and commit 2ee637a94c1abc09d0ab102e1f1a655a7292322d dropped the Request/Event instantiates data elements, while FHIR-40406 and commit 1e7ed5c7a6146f8bd69ebfb2169cd9c687d9e34d aligned the Definition pattern with CanonicalResource, leaving Definition.derivedFromCanonical and Definition.derivedFromUri. Current searches of source/definition, source/event, and source/request find no definitionReference or definitionUri elements.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source should not be edited for FHIR-13908: Definition carries the later canonical/uri derivedFrom representation, and Request/Event no longer carry instantiates data elements because of later final workflow history.
